error.vault_not_allowed: Home Assistant isn't allowed to write there. Add the folder to allowlist_external_dirs in configuration.yaml.
error.vault_not_writable: Home Assistant can't write to that folder.

error.calendar_invalid_link: That isn't a calendar link. Copy the whole link, starting with https://.

init.title: Hey Auri Client options
init.description: Choose which settings group to edit.

guest.title: Guest settings
guest.description: Booking details, and what Auri tells guests.{calendar_booking}{stated_name}

data_description.guest_name: Leave it empty and Auri asks the guests their name once during the stay, and keeps their answer for that stay only. A name you enter here is always used instead.
data_description.guest_phone_number: Only US/Canada numbers are supported. Use +1 format (for example, +16045551234) or a 10-digit local number (for example, 6045551234).
data_description.property_knowledge: Where non-IoT items are and how to use them. Example: Extra towels are in the hallway linen closet on the second shelf. Used towels should be placed in the laundry basket in the bathroom before checkout.
data_description.local_recommendations: What is around the house. Example: For coffee, the host recommends Corner Bean Cafe on West 4th Avenue. It is a cozy local coffee shop that is good for morning coffee, pastries, and a quick breakfast before heading out. It is usually quieter before 9 AM.
data_description.guest_memory_enabled: In guest mode, Auri remembers what guests tell it and learns from their conversations each night, for this stay only. It's kept apart from your own memory, in your PostgreSQL database (Memory must be set up). Erased an hour after check-out (then closed until the next booking), and started again for each new booking ID (or new check-in when there's no booking ID).
data_description.reset_guest_memory: Erase all guest memory now and start again from the guest name, guest count, check-in and check-out, and notes above.

booking_calendar.title: Booking calendar
booking_calendar.description: With your listing's calendar link, Auri fills in the booking ID, check-in and check-out of each booking in the Guest options by itself. It checks for changes every 30 minutes and moves to the next booking an hour after each check-out.{calendar_booking}

data_description.booking_calendar_url: Optional. Your Airbnb calendar's export link (on Airbnb: Calendar → Availability → Connect calendars → Export calendar), or any other iCal link. A new link starts afresh from its own calendar. Clear it to enter bookings yourself in the Guest options.
data_description.usual_check_in_time: Airbnb's calendar has dates but no times, so Auri uses this one for every booking.
data_description.usual_check_out_time: Used the same way for check-out. Guests keep their details and guest memory until an hour after it.

memory.title: Memory
memory.description: Let Auri remember facts, preferences and past conversations in owner mode, stored in your own PostgreSQL database (with the pgvector extension). Each night the day's conversation is sent to Auri's backend to be summarized; it isn't kept there. Saving tests the connection without changing anything.

data.memory_vault_include_private: Include private memories in the vault copy

data_description.memory_db_host: For the TimescaleDB app on Home Assistant OS: 77b2833f-timescaledb.
data_description.memory_db_password: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
data_description.memory_vault_path: Auri keeps a readable copy here (Auri/Daily notes and Auri/Memory.md), for example /share/AuriVault. Edits made in the vault aren't read back.
data_description.memory_day_boundary_hour: Conversation before this hour counts toward the previous day. Each day is processed about 15 minutes after it ends.
data_description.memory_share_household: Auri uses everyone's memories, private ones too, whoever is speaking, including an unknown speaker on a voice satellite. Anyone near a satellite could hear them, visitors too.

logins.title: Who uses each login
logins.description: When someone uses Assist signed in to Home Assistant, Auri uses the memories of the person their login is linked to. Choose someone else if another person uses a login (for example, you sign in as admin). Choose Shared for a login the household shares, like a wall tablet: Auri then treats the speaker as unknown, as on a voice satellite. Choose Not a person for a login a service uses, like Zigbee2MQTT's MQTT login: its person isn't counted as a household member. Nothing changes in Home Assistant.{preselected}

support.title: Auri support
support.description:
On a Home Assistant that Auri set up for you, Auri support has an account of its own, to help you remotely. Each time it signs in, you're told: a notification here in Home Assistant and on the phones with the Home Assistant app. Each sign-in also ends by itself 12 hours later, so nobody at Auri stays signed in.

Until you choose here, the account whose username is support counts as Auri support's. Choose None if Auri didn't set up this Home Assistant.

service_logins.title: Some logins look like services, not people

logins.title: Who uses each login
logins.description:
Auri counts the person of each Home Assistant login as a household member, so a login that a service or a device uses, like Zigbee2MQTT's MQTT login, should be Not a person.

**Set to Not a person, because the name looks like a service's or a device's:** {logins}. If one is someone's own login, choose their person instead. Choose Shared for a login the household shares, like a wall tablet. Nothing changes in Home Assistant.

similar_names.title: Auri may know one pet or person under two names

names.title: Names spelled two ways
names.description:
Speech-to-text sometimes spells a name differently from one time to the next, and Auri then remembers two pets or people where there's one. These names are a letter or so apart: {names}.

For each, choose whether it's the same one, and how it's spelled, or two. The same one keeps both spellings, so either name finds it, and everything Auri remembers about each is kept. Leave Not sure yet to be asked again later.

remote_logins_without_two_factor.title: Accounts can sign in from the internet with a password alone
remote_logins_without_two_factor.description:
Home Assistant can be reached from outside your home (remote access), so its login page is on the internet. These accounts can sign in there with only a password: {accounts}.

Turn on two-factor login for each one. Sign in as that person, open their profile (their name at the bottom of the sidebar), choose **Security**, and under **Multi-factor authentication modules** enable **Authenticator app**, then scan the code with an authenticator app on their phone. Signing in on a new phone or browser then also asks for the app's code; phones and browsers already signed in stay signed in.

An account that never needs remote access can be limited to the home network instead: **Settings** → **People**, choose the person, and turn on **Local access only**.

This notice goes away within an hour once every account listed has two-factor login or local access only.

remote_login_lockout_off.title: Failed logins never lock anyone out
remote_login_lockout_off.description:
Home Assistant can be reached from outside your home (remote access), and anyone can try passwords on its login page without limit: no address is banned after failed logins.

In **Settings** → **System** → **Network**, under **HTTP server**, turn on **Enable IP banning** and set **Login attempts before ban**, for example to 5.

Behind a tunnel or another reverse proxy, also turn on **Trust X-Forwarded-For** and add the proxy under **Trusted proxies** (for the Cloudflared add-on, 172.30.33.0/24). Otherwise Home Assistant sees every remote login as coming from the proxy, and a ban would lock out everyone using remote access.

Banned addresses are listed in ip_bans.yaml in the configuration folder: delete a line and restart Home Assistant to let that address in again.

old_timer_automation.title: The automation that rang Auri's timers isn't needed anymore

confirm.title: Delete the old timer automation
confirm.description:
Hey Auri Client now rings timers by itself: a voice satellite rings with its LED countdown, and a timer set from the phone app notifies that phone. The automation that rang them before, {automations}, no longer runs, since the event it waits for isn't sent anymore.

Submit to delete it. Your other automations stay as they are.

abort.gone: The old timer automation has been deleted already.
